summary: El Dorado County enclosed tower: 1958 as-built plans, replacing a 1935 CCC lookout; volunteer-staffed since its 2019 reopening. Sources disagree on the build year.

facts.design: Enclosed tower based on the revised 809R plan, with a few deviations; aluminum sheeting, angled cab windows and steel mullions

access.note: Register: not readily accessible to the public; about 1.5 miles from a paved road, behind a private subdivision and security gate (note marked MVT 10/91)

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

events.note: CCC lookout on the site, later replaced by the present building
As-built plans (Plan No. 237) drawn up in 1958; building believed to date from the Folsom Dam project
Registered March 16, 2015 as US 1065, CA 106; nominated by Al Ramirez
CAL FIRE repairs and renovations completed; tower reopened June 2019
Reopened staffed entirely by volunteers, mostly on 6 to 12 hour shifts

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register dates the as-built plans to 1958 and says the building is believed to date from the Folsom Dam project; Peakbagging gives 1985 for the Folsom Dam project tower. The story uses the Register's more specific 1958 date and reports the disagreement.
NHLR and FFLOS agree on 38.818 N, -121.030 W, which matches the record. The west_us_lookouts point in the brief (38.83441, -121.01418) is about 2 km away and is not used.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict (1958 Register vs 1985 Peakbagging) is unresolved; the story says so. The Pilot Peak name is linked to this tower by matching descriptions (CAL FIRE list, CBS report, Peakbagging page), not by a source that states it outright. CBS report has no date on the cached copy. mtdemocrat.com article on CAL FIRE bringing four towers back into use returned HTTP 429 twice and is not used; it may be worth a retry. A CAL FIRE Amador-El Dorado post in search results mentions the Pilot Hill lookout spotting a fire; not fetched, so not used. Access is recorded as restricted from a 10/91 note in the NHLR and may be out of date.
